fixes.what: One rule for the 'Par / Units' figure of LP, LLC, specialty-finance and fund-interest rows (round 2, after the orchestrator found two readings). The 10-Q for 2026-03-31 splits the column into 'Par' and 'Unit': every such interest prints its figure under Par with a dash under Unit (Chrome 8,754; Project Alpine 6,667; Credit SLF 16,161; Stripe 7,797; Leasing 350), while counts print under Unit (Nscale preferred equity '- 3,038', Snowbird '- 393,246', Rome Topco '- 3,127,449'), and the commitments table prints the same figures as the '$' funded commitment ('Chrome Investors LP LP Interest N/A $ 8,754 $ 2,189'). The '$' the 2025 10-Qs print is the dollar sign of that par: in the four 10-Qs scanned (2025-03-31, 2025-09-30, 2025-12-31, 2026-03-31) no warrant, common-unit or preferred-share count carries one. So a figure printed in thousands that is the par is not a count: no unit count is published (Nscale preferred equity '$ 3,346' included, unchanged); a full count printed as such (Project Alpine 6,666,667 at 2023-12-31, Hotel California 6,711,769) stays a count. Applied: the 37 counts I had set on such rows in round 1 (30 row corrections, 7 through added wrapper labels) are withdrawn; the wrapper labels are back to 'LLC Interest' only; counts withdrawn by row correction (empty value) on Project Alpine 2023-03-31, Credit SLF 2024-12-31, Blue Owl Leasing and Stripe 2026-03-31; Credit SLF 2026-03-31, set to 16,161,000 units by D-102, withdrawn by changing that D-102 entry in make_row_corrections.py and row_corrections.csv. Earlier-published counts of the same kind that the filer tagged as shares are left and listed under observations.
